all_feed.description: Every consecutive pair of collected last-traded-price observations for a market in the snapshot whose absolute change is >= swing_threshold_dollars, in either direction. Same rule as the dashboard feed (dashboard.html, renderAlerts).

high_roi.description: EXPERIMENTAL SCREEN, NOT AN ROI MODEL. Identical to the dashboard's 'Model watch' filter: category_basis == 'seed' (series in the official fee schedule) and volume_24h_fp > 0. The owner's model was not supplied (F-14).
high_roi.decided_at: detection time — build_alerts.py applies this screen to the snapshot it is reading and the archive is append-only, so the flag is a record of that moment and is never relabelled later. validate_alerts.py therefore checks each flag against the volume_24h_fp / category_basis stored with the alert, and reports disagreement with the current snapshot as drift (volume_24h_fp legitimately changes between collections) instead of failing the collector — see F-39 and scripts/tests/test_alerts.py HighRoiFreezeTests.

sources.price_observations: data/live/price_history.json (written by scripts/collect.py from GET /markets last_price_dollars)

evidence.description: T66 evidence layer. Every alert is classified by whether contracts actually traded between its two observations. Kalshi documents last_price_dollars as the price of the last TRADED contract and volume_fp as the market volume in contracts (https://docs.kalshi.com/api-reference/market/get-markets), so the difference of volume_fp across two reads is the number of contracts traded between them. A swing whose interval traded ZERO contracts is labelled quote_only: the reported last price changed with no trade at all.
evidence.floor_note: PROJECT RULE, NOT A KALSHI FIELD. Kalshi publishes no per-move significance field. The floor only decides which alert chip reads 'traded' rather than 'thin'; every alert still displays its exact contract count so a reader can apply their own threshold.
evidence.candle_note: A candidate state added mid-session: candlestick volume_fp is documented as the number of contracts bought DURING the candlestick period (https://docs.kalshi.com/api-reference/market/get-market-candlesticks), whereas GET /markets volume_fp is the market's cumulative volume in contracts. Differencing a candle point against a REST read would subtract unlike quantities, so such a swing is labelled candle_unquantified with a null count.

quote_check.description: 49BA-1 quote check. last_price_dollars is the last TRADED price; yes_bid_dollars and yes_ask_dollars are the two-sided quote of the SAME Get Markets read (https://docs.kalshi.com/api-reference/market/get-markets, documented as cached and able to lag the exchange). Every alert therefore also records evidence.quote: inside_quote when the printed end price sits within [to_yes_bid, to_yes_ask], outside_quote when it does not (with outside_by_dollars and the spread), unknown_quote when no usable quote was recorded with the read. It is a comparison of two recorded official fields, it does not claim why the two differ, and it does not re-score the frozen high_roi flag (that remains the owner's decision, F-26/F-77).
quote_check.published_as: data/live/alerts.json -> counts.quote_check (computed over the served rows by scripts/alert_evidence.py summarize_quote)
